thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging Mike (oncall) — GPU pool 'inference-west' reporting 95% queue growth and pod OOM throttles. Alert: GPU capacity_exhaustion_high.

mike_oncall: on it. seeing big token queue on the ML queue. which autoscaler is attached?

sara_sre: HPA for inference-worker in 'inference' ns. metrics from prometheus-adapter look delayed. last scrape full push at +2m. autoscale events not firing.

pranav_ml: confirming — prometheus-adapter logs show backlog + error 429s to metrics-server. looks like adapter -> metrics-server requests are timing out.

amy_engineer: customers hitting 503-ish latencies? any direct customer impact yet?

linda_cs: just got one customer message: "inference requests timeout or queue for minutes" for an enterprise account. escalated to enterprise SRE.

mike_oncall: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) temporarily scale inference-worker replicas manually to relieve queue (kubectl scale). 2) route some traffic to dedicated pool (if config available). 3) restart prometheus-adapter or increase its replicas to clear backlog. thoughts?

sara_sre: agree. first do manual scale out to avoid token loss. But note HPA maxReplicas currently 50; we might need 80. we need approval for bump to avoid race with quota.

pranav_ml: I can bump adapter replicas and restart metrics-server. but adapter restarts may lose pending metrics; better to add replicas first. I'm on it.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline started by pr/infra/quick-fix-metrics (build 9032).

amy_engineer: I'll open a temporary canary routing rule to send low-priority traffic to dedicated-pool-west. config patch applied:
```yaml
route: /v1/generate
weight: low-priority -> 0.3
fallback: dedicated-pool-west
```

mike_oncall: scaling inference-worker to 80 replicas now: `kubectl scale deployment/inference-worker --replicas=80 -n inference`

sara_sre: seeing pods come up. GPU util per-pod dropping from 99% -> 70%. queue length slowly falling.

pranav_ml: increased prometheus-adapter to 4 replicas and restarted metrics-server. adapter logs show backlog drain: `queue_length=0` around +90s. but I see multiple 403 from prometheus to metrics-server due to token rotation happening earlier — rotating certs blocked some requests. investigating token rotation window.

incident-bot: Note: Incident severity escalated to SEV2 due to customer impact and failed autoscale.

linda_cs: notified affected customers with status update. added ETA: 30m recovery window.

amy_engineer: I placed a temporary quota increase on the HPA controller: `maxReplicas: 120` in a hotfix; will monitor.

pranav_ml: found culprit: cron job rotated service-account token and the adapter didn't pick up new token because its sidecar token-sync failed. applied restart to token-sync sidecar and adapter is green. putting fwd an operator fix.

mike_oncall: good. now reduce manual replicas back to HPA control? wait until one full metric cycle confirms adapter stability.

sara_sre: agreed. hold manual scale for another 6 minutes. autoscaler metrics now showing correct target CPU/GPU custom metric.

deploy-bot: hotfix applied: infra/patch/adapter-token-reload merged.

pranav_ml: metrics pipeline stabilized. HPA scaled down from 80 -> 45 naturally over 7 minutes. queue length normalizing.

linda_cs: updated customers: service restored, some requests retried; offered credits for impacted windows.

amy_engineer: next steps: postmortem, add readiness probe to token-sync, make adapter metrics queue alert stricter, and add runbook step to increase HPA maxReplicas automatically when queue breach > 5m.

mike_oncall: I’ll own the postmortem. tagging Sara and Pranav for technical writeup. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved by mitigation and hotfix. Closing SEV2 state to monitoring.
